title: Against the worm in the bone

plan.english: Great worm, you who eat the bone, die! Worm, you who indeed drink the blood, vanish! And then let fire burn you; then let the sun dry you. Let the bird seize you. And now come out of the sinew! Come out of the bone! Do not devour the sinew.

Now: bone, blood and sinew. Let bone be joined with bone. Let blood be joined with blood. Let sinew be joined with sinew. And now the bone that broke, let it stand up again. Great Mother Earth, take the pain from the bone. Let him who lies there stand up; let him walk.

Blood, stand still! Blood, do not go out! Now the spear that wounded you, let it be broken. Let the red blood indeed stand in the sinew. Father Sky, hear this word! Now protect him, and let him become strong!
Fire in the bones, run into the water! Let it grow cold in the great bone. Let the cold come, then let what is warm flee. Let him sweat, let him drink and be satisfied. Let him not tremble.

Great heart, do not tremble! Heart, do not be afraid! Grief, indeed go out of the heart. Dawn and Sun, drive the grief out of the heart. And then let sleep come to him. Let the tears indeed dry up. Now let him become joyful.

title: A mother's charm for her son

plan.english: Son, do not die! Live; grow! Your mother protects you. May Sky and Earth guard you. And then let the suffering go to the wolf. Let the great wild beast eat it. Death, pass him by! Now, Dyeus, giver of good things, give him power.
Wolf, do not seize the lamb! Dog, guard the herd. Shepherd, lead the cattle home. And let the wild beast indeed not come near. Then let the wool grow. Dog, be awake. And now let the sheep grow full.
Now, snake, lie down! Indeed do not seize this man! Snake, you who indeed creep in the night, do not rise! Now, Perkunos, strike the snake with your spear. Snake, flee! Now let the snake go away.

Sleep, brother of death, indeed come! Let the good dog lie down, let the sheep lie down, let the bird lie down. Let the household lie down. Thief, do not come in the night. Night, cover us. And then may we wake at dawn.
The fire burned the man's arm. Let the arm grow cold. Smear the grease on the arm. Now let the grease heal the arm. Cold, indeed go to the arm. Let the arm become strong.

Swelling, indeed do not swell! Swelling, go down! And now, swelling, melt! Let the swift water carry the swelling away. And then let the cold seize the swelling. And let the wild beast devour the swelling, and let him live.
Who indeed wounded you? Who split your bone? Then the spear wounded me. The spear split it. I heal you; I smear the grease. Let the bone grow. Man, stand up!
Now, Dawn, you who drive the wheel of the sun, shine! Night, go away! Let the suffering flee with the darkness. Let the bird indeed wake. Now, Dawn, let him see you.
Let him live a hundred years! Let death pass him by. Then let the gods make him grow old. Sun, look on him. And now let his horses grow. May he become rich in livestock.

Hero, you who drove cattle, you who overpowered the snake, you have died. Now you lie in the field. Your sister weeps. And grief indeed has seized your wife. We clothe you in a garment. And now your fame is imperishable.
Son, you left me. I nursed you; you are my heart. I hold your garment. I weep for you by night. Now, Mother Earth, take my son.
Brother, you drove the cattle and you gave me a share. And then you protected your sister. Who now gives me a share? I sit in the darkness. You are dead; I weep. Your name is indeed famous among men.
Father, you indeed led us and gave us horses. You indeed protected us; we remember you. Cold has seized us. We sit and cry. Who now speaks for us and then leads us?
Husband, you went away; you did not come back. I wear your garment, and I look at your yoke. And now it is getting dark in the household. I seek you, and I remember you.
King, shepherd of men, you have indeed died. You guarded us; you gave us rewards. Now we sit around you. Then Dawn shines, but you do not stand up. Who is our king now?
Now, dead shepherd, you lie in the field. Your dog sits; it cries. It is getting dark; the sheep do not eat. The wolf approaches; no one guards them. Now your name is famous among men.

title: For a father full of years

plan.english: Old father, you have died. You saw many years, and then you knew the words of the old. You led us. You sat down, and you spoke to us. The gods have taken you. Your name is famous.

Son of good fame, swift one, you indeed did not grow old. You ran; the spear wounded you in the field. And your blood is now red on the field. And now we do not see you. And now death seized you. Your name is famous.

title: For a stranger who died among us

plan.english: Stranger, you indeed came to us and died. Now, stranger, who is your begetter? Where indeed is your mother? Cold seized you. We gave you swift water, but it did not heal you. Earth, take the stranger.

title: The horses of the dead charioteer

plan.english: He who drove you, swift horses, is dead. You two stand at the yoke, and no one has yoked you. And now the horses look for him. The horses indeed do not eat. The wheel stands still.

plan.english: Brother, I saw you falling. Then I stood near, and I did not protect you. I carried you from the field. The field drank your blood. Now I go away, and I indeed remember you. And your fame indeed is imperishable.

Hero, where indeed did you go away to? To Mother Earth I indeed went down. And who now drives your cattle? And now my brother-in-law drives them. Now who speaks your words? The king speaks them. What do you carry? I carry imperishable fame. It does not die.
Son, hear my word. A true word is good. Say the truth. Do not deceive a friend. Whoever speaks the truth is dear to the gods. The word that goes out does not come back. Hear, then speak.

Give the guest water and wine. He comes from Dyeus. Do not deceive him. Seat him at your table. Do not drive him out of your household. The household that gives to the guest is dear to the gods. The guest remembers the giver.
Guard your pledge. A pledge is great. Do not break the pledge. Father Sky sees. Whoever breaks a pledge, Perkunos strikes him. Whoever guards the pledge, his name is famous.

title: A father to his two sons

plan.english: Two sons, hear me. A brother is dear. Do not leave your brother. Two brothers are stout. Eat together, drink together. Whoever leaves him is a wolf.
Listen to the old. The old man is a knower. Whoever lives grows old. The old man knows much. Give the old man a seat. Clothe the old man in a garment. The old man sitting by the fire speaks.

title: A father on fire, water and night

plan.english: Water goes down; fire goes up. Fire and water are not friendly. The sun goes, and the night comes. Night covers the thief. Dawn follows it.

title: A father on what does not die

plan.english: Cattle die. Fathers die. A man dies. Fame does not die. The fame of the dead is imperishable. Seek good fame. Set yourself a famous name.

title: A father on wolf and thief

plan.english: The wolf is not dear to the sheep. The thief is not friendly to the household. The dog guards the sheep. The wolf comes by night. The thief creeps by night. Be awake by night. The shepherd who is not awake, his sheep are gone. Do not steal.
Work. Plough the field. Whoever ploughs, eats. Milk the cattle. Build the enclosure. Harness the horses. Whoever works takes his share.
Seek the truth. The knower is good. Whoever has seen much knows much. Whoever hears, learns. Do not hide the truth. The truth is dear.

title: A father on death

plan.english: Whoever lives, dies. The dead do not come back. Death takes the old and the swift. Do not weep for many nights. Grief goes, and the sun comes.

plan.english: Give worship to the gods. They are givers of good things. A libation is dear to them. They see the giver. Father Sky hears the giver. Do not deceive the gods. Mother Earth carries the men.

title: A father on friends and wine

plan.english: Wine makes the heart joyful. Drink wine with a friend. Do not deceive him. Give him your portion. The dog is dear to the shepherd. A man of ill fame is not friendly.
